category_title: Nonverbal students with ASD who engage in repetitive tapping or premature screen advancing during iPad-based instruction
minimal_context: The student is using an AAC app on an iPad during snack-time to request a snack from an adult partner.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is snack time. Please use your AAC app to request a snack.

STUDENT: (Taps the iPad screen but does not direct eye gaze or body orientation toward the adult.)

TUTOR: What would you like?

STUDENT: (Presses the screen again without looking at the adult or hesitating to await a response.)

TUTOR: Try telling me again.

STUDENT: (Continues to use the AAC app independently without directing any motoric act toward the adult or awaiting a response, violating the requirement for intentional communication.)

options.A: Put the student in a position where they are less distracted, so they are not seeing things.
options.B: Smile at the student's accomplishment and gently congratulate them on using the AAC app.
options.C: Serve as a communication partner during snack-time, requiring the student to request using the AAC app.
options.D: Ask 'why' in a caring manner, such as 'why are you just tapping the AAC app?'
